key_insight: Independent testing confirms that RXNGraphormer can be reproduced and works well across multiple reaction prediction tasks. However, its performance drops in heterogeneous and distribution-shifted datasets, highlighting limits to real-world transferability.
problem_solved: The paper addresses whether RXNGraphormer is truly reproducible and whether it remains reliable when evaluated on external datasets outside its original training or benchmark conditions.
method: Reproduced RXNGraphormer independently to verify whether reported results can be matched.
Evaluated the model on external benchmarks covering multiple reaction prediction tasks.
Compared performance under standard settings versus heterogeneous and distribution-shifted data conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides evidence that RXNGraphormer is a solid baseline for reaction prediction, but also a reminder that strong benchmark results may not guarantee robustness in deployment. It underscores the importance of external validation and shift-aware evaluation.

paper_title: Reusability report: Assessment of reproducibility and applicability to external datasets for RXNGraphormer
paper_authors: Chonghuan Zhang, Majian Zeng, Qianghua Lin, Kuangbiao Liao
